title: SDLC Analysis Run Manifest
description: Schema for '_run-manifest.json' at the root of a run directory. Written by the extract orchestrator at assembly from what the domain extractor agents returned through their marker blocks — never from record content, which the orchestrator does not see. '--resume <dir>' reads this file to decide which datasets to re-run. Prose contract: docs/output-contract.md.

run_id.description: The run directory's own name — a compact UTC timestamp, e.g. '20260714T093000Z'.

started_at.description: When the run began, verbatim — original UTC offset preserved, never normalised to Z.

completed_at.description: When assembly finished, verbatim. Null or absent for a run that has not finished, which is how a resumed run reads before its second pass completes.

plugin_version.description: Version from .claude-plugin/plugin.json, so a run can be read against the contract it was produced under.

invocation.description: The arguments this run was invoked with, echoed back so a run is reproducible from its own output.

domains.description: Domain shortnames selected by --domain. All four when the flag was absent.

resume.description: The run directory passed to --resume, or null for a fresh run.

window.description: The time window the run was asked for, and the bounds it resolved to. Each dataset's sidecar repeats this so a single file is self-describing.

requested.description: The window argument as the user gave it, e.g. '6m'.

from.description: Resolved start of the window, verbatim.

to.description: Resolved end of the window, verbatim.

scope.description: What the run covered, in the providers' own identifiers.

identifiers.description: Provider-native repository / project / service identifiers covered by the run. Empty array when no provider was connected at all.

note.description: How the scope was determined, when that is not obvious from the identifiers alone.

scope_selection.description: How the run's scope was decided. 'full' = every scope unit each resolved provider exposes (also how a manifest written before this field existed reads). 'curated' = the user enumerated and picked; per-domain entries record what was kept and — with evidence — what was deliberately left out. Deselected units appear in no dataset, so this object is the only place they remain visible. See docs/output-contract.md section 7.

mode.description: 'full' = full sweep. 'curated' = the user picked scope units per domain after enumeration.

note.description: Free-text qualifier, e.g. that a curated run fell back to a full sweep because enumeration failed.

domains.description: One entry per enumerated domain, keyed by shortname. Present only when mode is 'curated'.

enumeration.description: Whether the scope-scout's listing ran to exhaustion, hit the per-domain cap, or could not run.

selection.description: 'all' = the user kept everything; the domain extracts at provider default scope and carries no selected/deselected arrays. 'curated' = the user picked; both arrays are present.

reason.description: Why enumeration failed, in the provider's terms. Required when enumeration is 'failed'.

selected.description: The units this run extracts, exactly as passed to the domain extractor as scope_units.

deselected.description: The units deliberately left out, kept visible here with their evidence — exclusion is never silent.

reason.description: Why the unit was left out, e.g. 'user-deselected'.

output_guard.description: Evidence that the output directory was checked before any record was written. Records carry author identities and ticket summaries and are never redacted, so placement is the guard.

path.description: The output directory the guard was run against.

git_ignored.description: Result of 'git check-ignore' on the output directory.

warned.description: Whether the user was warned that the path is tracked.

confirmed_by_user.description: Whether the user explicitly confirmed writing to a tracked path. Required when git_ignored is false.

domains.description: One entry per selected domain. A domain whose agent failed, returned nothing, or emitted no markers appears here as 'unavailable' with a reason — never as a missing key and never as an aborted run.

domain.description: Domain shortname: a = version control, b = CI/CD, c = tickets, d = incidents.

status.description: 'resolved' = a provider was found and the agent reported back. 'unavailable' = no provider was connected, or the agent returned nothing usable.

name.description: Provider identifier resolved for this domain, e.g. 'github', 'azure-devops', 'jira', 'pagerduty'. Null when status is 'unavailable'.

detected_via.description: Which detection surface found it — MCP tools present, or a CLI on PATH. Null exactly when name is null: an unconnected provider was detected via nothing.

reason.description: Why the domain is unavailable, in concrete terms. Required when status is 'unavailable'.

datasets.description: Per-dataset completeness for every dataset the run has a sidecar for, copied from those sidecars, except truncation_count which is derived (see below). This is what --resume reads: it re-runs exactly the datasets whose sidecar is absent or not 'complete'. The array's length is not fixed at 24 or at the selected domains' full range — a --resume run legitimately covers only the datasets it re-ran plus whatever sidecars were already on disk.

dataset.description: Lowercase dataset id, one of the 24 in docs/output-contract.md section 2.

completeness.description: Same closed three-state enum as the sidecar's, copied from it verbatim.

record_count.description: Line count of the dataset's JSONL, copied from the sidecar.

truncation_count.description: How many truncation records the sidecar carries, so a reader sees which datasets need --resume without opening every sidecar. NOT copied — the sidecar has no truncation_count field. It is derived as the length of that sidecar's 'truncation' array (truncation.length), 0 for an empty array. The count lives only here, as a run-level roll-up; duplicating it into the sidecar would give truncation.length a second home to drift from. See docs/output-contract.md section 7.

gaps_file.description: Filename of the run's gaps document. Always 'gaps.md'.

id.description: Provider-native identifier of the unit — a repository, pipeline, board / project, or service.

name.description: Display name as the provider's listing reported it.

last_activity.description: Last-activity timestamp copied verbatim from the provider's listing response by the scope-scout. Absent when the listing carried none — never null, never computed.
